conceptZh: 發條樂團的小號手拿到過長的樂器，樂器彎折成七。
object: a wind-up animal band with an oversized trumpet and a tiny triangle
morph: an absurdly long bendy trumpet folds into the strokes of 七
creativeAngle: 大小懸殊：小熊貓鼓手拿到比自己長三倍的喇叭，折彎後恰好成為七；七彩的氣球從喇叭口噴出呼應「七彩」。
promptEn:
An 8-second bouncy animated clip on a warm peach backdrop with a pale lemon floor. A wind-up red-panda trumpeter, key turning on its back, struggles with a trumpet three times longer than itself, while a mouse with a tiny triangle watches. The off-screen voice, warm and clear Taiwanese Mandarin, says exactly: 「七、七、七彩」 (ㄑㄧ、ㄑㄧ、ㄑㄧ ㄘㄞˇ), slowly with clear tones, then stops.
0.0-1.7s: The panda inhales and blows; the huge trumpet swings like a crane, knocking the cymbals over with a clang. 「七」 (ㄑㄧ) is spoken as the trumpet swings.
1.7-3.4s: The panda tries to fit it on stage, so he bends it; the trumpet folds with a boing, a short flat top bar and a long hooked tail, forming one deep violet glyph 七, saturated solid strokes, filling about 70% of frame height. The second 「七」 (ㄑㄧ) lands as it settles.
3.4-5.0s: The panda blows once more and the bell of the folded horn burps out seven balloons in seven rainbow colors that float up behind the glyph; 「七彩」 (ㄑㄧ ㄘㄞˇ) is spoken as the colorful balloons pop out.
5.0-8.0s: Hold: glyph 七 absolutely still, centered, uncropped. The panda hugs the horn base and sways, the mouse dings its tiny triangle, away from the strokes.
Only the glyph 七 appears as text; no subtitles, watermark or flashing. Light music below the voice.

conceptZh: 玩具戰士想一劍掃倒花生排好的七塊積木，結果揮太用力自己轉圈，盾牌輕輕碰倒第一塊，七塊積木骨牌般連環倒下，排成長長的彎鉤；最後一塊壓下翹板把戰士彈上天，他的泡棉劍掉下來橫在上面變成一橫，七就完成了。
object: a row of seven chunky deep-red toy blocks standing along a hockey-stick path, plus the warrior's red foam sword
morph: the seven blocks topple one after another and lie end-to-end as one continuous solid stroke that runs straight down, bends right and curls up into a hook; the flying foam sword drops flat across the upper part of that stroke as the horizontal bar, completing 七
creativeAngle: 與前一版（小號彎成七）完全不同：改用骨牌連鎖的實體笑料。七塊積木剛好對應「七個」，倒下後拼成豎彎鉤，泡棉劍落下成一橫，筆畫由撞擊本身排出來。戰士「用力過猛轉圈反而輕碰」是角色性格驅動的失誤；花生在錯誤時機敬禮負責收尾的數數畫面。選詞「七個」因為畫面上正好有七塊積木，且「個」只有一個讀音。
promptEn:
An 8-second bouncy stylized toy-animation clip, bright and clean: a pale butter-yellow backdrop and a soft cream floor, nothing busy behind. Only two characters: the lead is a chunky teal-armored toy warrior with a yellow plume, a round orange shield strapped to his back and a fat red foam sword, all bravado and very little skill. His buddy is Peanut, a small cartoon raccoon sidekick with a striped tail. In the center of the frame stand seven chunky deep-red toy blocks in a neat row along a hockey-stick path: straight down the middle of the frame, bending to the right at the bottom, the last block resting on a tiny cream seesaw plank. The teaching subject stays centered and uncropped at all times.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「七、七、七個」 (ㄑㄧ、ㄑㄧ、ㄑㄧ ㄍㄜˋ), reading exactly those syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops. No other dialogue, no subtitles, no on-screen text except the finished glyph. Soft toy-box music kept well below the voice.

0.0–1.5s: Peanut has just set down the last block and salutes proudly at nothing. The warrior stamps in from the left, points his foam sword at the row of seven blocks, puffs out his chest and winds up a huge two-handed swing, sword pulled way back behind his head, eyes squeezed shut with effort.

1.5–3.0s: He swings so hard he whirls around twice like a top, misses every block completely, and staggers dizzy with crossed eyes. As he wobbles, the round shield on his back gives the first block the gentlest little tap. The first 「七」 (ㄑㄧ) is spoken exactly as that first block tips with a soft click. Peanut's jaw drops.

3.0–4.5s: Domino chain, faster and faster: clack, clack, clackclackclack, each block knocking the next down the straight run and around the bend, and together they lie end-to-end as one continuous thick solid deep-red stroke that runs straight down, bends right and curls up into a hook. The seventh block slams the seesaw plank, which flips the warrior straight up into the air with a boing; his red foam sword flies loose, tumbles once, and drops flat across the upper part of the standing stroke as a clean horizontal bar. The second 「七」 (ㄑㄧ) lands exactly as the sword settles and the glyph 七 snaps complete: one correctly formed Traditional Chinese 七, a horizontal bar crossed by a vertical stroke that bends right and ends in an upturned hook, solid saturated deep red on the pale background, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. The warrior plops down bottom-first on the floor just past the hook's tip with a cartoon squash, bounces once, and stares at what he did.

4.5–8.0s: Final hold. The glyph 七 stays perfectly still and readable, centered and uncropped, nothing touching or covering the strokes. At 4.5s the dazed warrior slowly raises a surprised thumbs-up. At about 5.0s 「七個」 (ㄑㄧ ㄍㄜˋ) is spoken exactly as Peanut, on the far left away from the strokes, holds up both paws and seven small pale-yellow dots pop up one by one in a quick arc above his head, then he salutes at the wrong moment again. The warrior keeps living in the lower right corner: a wobbly victory wiggle, a dizzy spin on one foot, and a proud chest-puff, never near the glyph. Soft, warm lighting throughout; no neon, no white blowouts, no watermark, no flashing effects, no extra text.
